title: Zeabur shutting down after second security breach in two months
description: Zeabur, a developer hosting and deployment platform, suffered a second security breach within two months. Attackers used leaked internal credentials stored in plaintext to compromise infrastructure, stealing over 3.2 million environment variable records and data for 321,810 accounts. The breach involved unauthorized root access to multiple servers and the addition of SSH keys by attackers. Zeabur failed to rotate administrator credentials after the first breach and left admin portals publicly accessible. Following this incident, Zeabur announced it will shut down its services by the end of 2026.
aiSummary: In October 2026, Zeabur disclosed a cybersecurity incident where attackers leveraged leaked internal credentials, stored in plaintext and not rotated since January 2024, to compromise shared clusters and dedicated servers across nine regions. The attackers accessed the production database, stealing over 3.2 million environment variable records and information for 321,810 accounts. They performed root sign-ins on 101 Google Cloud Platform servers, added SSH keys to 50 servers, and attached 16 customer disk copies to their own virtual machines. The credentials used were likely obtained during an earlier August 2026 breach, where attackers exploited a flaw in a customer's application and moved laterally through poorly isolated internal systems. Zeabur's failure to rotate admin tokens and secure admin portals contributed to the severity of the breach. In response, Zeabur decided to shut down its platform by December 31, 2026.
aiImpact: The breach resulted in the theft of sensitive environment variables and account information for over 321,000 users, potentially exposing API keys, secrets, and other confidential data. Attackers gained root access to multiple cloud servers and compromised infrastructure integrity. The exposure of plaintext internal credentials and failure to rotate them increased the attack surface and facilitated the breach. The incident forced Zeabur to cease operations, impacting its user base and service availability.
